title: Runtime Reference: Execution Location Switching
summary: Runtime Reference acts as the execution-location switch, allowing a semantic operation to be bound to a local or remote implementation without the caller's knowledge.
why: Enables deployment flexibility; an operation can be shifted to a remote node for scaling or specialized hardware without changing the calling code.
invariants: The caller invokes the same class and method; the deployment binds the semantic operation to a resident or remote implementation.
The owning package retains its native ooRexx implementation as a fallback.
Runtime Reference is separate from Runtime Registry: Registry selects the module generation; Reference selects where that operation executes.
